                                                    14         II.       AFFIRMATIVE DEFENSES

                                                    15                   A. NO BREACH

                                                    16         5. Defendant acknowledges the requirement set forth by Congress to mandate the Affidavit

                                                    17               of Support in immigration cases. Defendant understands that visa petitioners, such as

                                                    18               himself, are expected to act as a financial safety net for the new immigrants they sponsor.

                                                    19               Defendant states that if the court finds the Affidavit of Support valid, he has a responsibility

                                                    20               to provide the equivalent of 125 percent of the Federal Poverty Guidelines.

                                                    21         6. Defendant has made every effort to fulfill the duty as the sponsor under the Affidavit of

                                                    22               Support. Defendant has provided the Plaintiffs a monthly cash allowance and pays for the

                                                    23               Plaintiffs’ health insurance, tuition, supplies, auto-insurance, car payments, cell phone,

                                                    24               internet, transportation, and other living costs. He believes these living expenses Defendant

                                                    25               has covered for the Plaintiffs constitute as income.

                                                     5            App'x 532 (9th Cir. 2019).

                                                     9            married him for the immigration benefit. Once married, Plaintiff Akiko’s behavior has

                                                    10            shown she never intended to engage in a marital relationship. They married in a courthouse

                                                    11            in Japan with none of their family members present. Defendant has only seen Plaintiff

                                                    12            Akiko wear the wedding ring twice – at the store when he purchased it for her and at a

                                                    13            dinner with her parents. Plaintiff Akiko and Defendant have not consummated the

                                                    21            lawful permanent resident status. If Plaintiffs as the intended beneficiaries lied to

                                                     7              not provide a protection of a sponsoring spouse from the abuse of a sponsored immigrant
